payload.label: Change one piece of text in a file
payload.job: Change one exact piece of text in a text or code file without sending the whole file: give the words to find and the words to put there
payload.description: Give file (a path inside the folder the person granted for change), find (the exact text, as it is in the file, newlines and quotes included) and replace (what to put there; empty removes the found text). The find text must occur exactly once: no match or more than one is refused and nothing is written, so a change that did not happen is never reported as done. Bytes are compared as they are: no pattern, no case folding, no whitespace tolerance. The file is replaced in one step after the full new text is written, keeps its permissions, and is left alone if it changed while the edit was prepared. A path that leaves the folder, goes through a link, is a folder or is not UTF-8 text is refused. Returns the file, its size before and after, and replaced: 1.

file.description: Path relative to the granted folder

find.description: The exact text to find; it must occur exactly once in the file

replace.description: The text to put in its place; may be empty

payload.label: Change several pieces of text in files, all or nothing
payload.job: Make several exact text changes across one or more text or code files in one go, so either every change is made or none is
payload.description: Give edits: a list of { file, find, replace }, each as in tool:replace-one-piece-of-text-in-a-file. They apply in order, and a later edit to the same file sees the text the earlier ones made. Every find must occur exactly once at the moment its edit applies; if any edit is refused (no match, more than one, a path that leaves the folder, goes through a link, is a folder or is not UTF-8 text) nothing is written to any file and the refusal names the edit by its place in the list. Every changed file is written beside itself first and all are put in place only when none of them changed while the edits were prepared; each keeps its permissions. Returns each file changed with its size before and after and how many edits it took, and the number of edits. A person can also keep the edits in a JSON file and run the script with that file after the folder.

file.description: Path relative to the granted folder

find.description: The exact text to find; it must occur exactly once in the file

replace.description: The text to put in its place; may be empty
